children: WTI crude was on track for an eighth straight day of gains, its longest winning streak in more than three years, as the Iran conflict continued to fuel concerns over oil supplies.
October WTI futures were up 0.87% at $96.89, according to the Barchart chart.

The rally came as the conflict between the U.S. and Iran continued to escalate, putting the Strait of Hormuz firmly in focus for energy markets. The waterway is a critical route for global oil shipments, making any disruption from the conflict a direct concern for crude supplies.

The latest stretch of gains had taken WTI sharply higher from its recent lows. The chart showed the contract moving steadily higher through late August before accelerating in September, with gains recorded in each of the past seven sessions.
WTI had climbed through the $90 level during the latest leg higher and was trading near $97 on Thursday, putting it at the highest level shown on the chart.

The sustained advance reflected the growing supply risk surrounding the Iran conflict, particularly as fighting and tensions around Hormuz raised concerns about how much oil could continue moving through the region.
If Thursday's gains held, WTI would record its eighth consecutive green session, giving crude its longest winning streak in more than three years, according to Barchart.
